_about: Purchased parts for the mates_task_v2 brief (pan-tilt). Dimensions in mm. Placeholders: kit_parts.py builds each in the local frame its "frame" line gives; use them unmodified (don't cut or join them): the scorer finds each by its mesh. Tapped holes are not modelled in the placeholders (a screw into one is style 'tapped' with the depth below). connectors: named frames in that local frame for cadlib.mates (mates.from_component): origin on the mating face, z out of the part, x in the face (default: the frame's +X flattened into the face, +Z when z is along X), a hole pattern in minimal form (["rect", px, py] along the connector's x and y, ["circle", pcd, n, a0_deg]) seen from outside the face, and the hole size.

servo.what: Bus servo, HTS-35H class; two are used (pan and tilt)
servo.frame: origin on the spline axis at the case top; spline up +Z; case below z = 0; the case's 40 mm length along X with its centre at x = -10; 20 mm width along Y

side.about: centre of the case's -Y face (the 40 x 40 face), 28 along X and 28 along Z

servo.src: components/components.json hiwonder_bus_servo (drawing); tapped holes per the kit

spline.note: spline top: the horn hub seats here and turns about z

bottom.note: case bottom centre; tapped M2.5, 5 deep

side.note: the -Y face's centre; tapped M2.5, 5 deep (connector y is the servo's +Z)

horn.what: Round 8-hole servo horn; two are used
horn.frame: origin on the axis at the hub underside (on the spline top); disc above; hole 0 on +X

hub.note: hub underside, on the spline top

face_4.note: disc top, every other hole (0, 90, 180, 270 deg)

camera.what: Camera board, 25 x 24 x 1.0, lens on the front, 4 x M2 holes
camera.frame: origin at the lens centre on the board's back face; the lens looks along +Z; board 'up' is +Y; the board spans x -12.5..12.5, y -14..10, z 0..1; lens d 8 from z 1 to 6

holes.about: the hole pattern's centre is 3 mm below the lens

back.note: board back at the hole-pattern centre

front.note: board front: screw heads bear here

optical.note: on the lens axis at the board back; z along the optical axis
